description:
Who holds a company, from 13F filings: how much of each share class institutions hold,
and how that changed quarter by quarter. The company-side view of 13F; get_holdings is the
manager side (what one institution owns).

Use it for questions like:
  - "What % of AMD do institutions hold, and how has it changed over the last 4 quarters?"
    -> quarters=4; read quarters[].share_classes[].pct_of_class.
  - "Is Baupost an investor in AMD?" -> holder="Baupost" (a name fragment or a filer CIK).
    holder.matched_filers says which filers the name matched (empty: no 13F filer has
    it), holder.positions each quarter's position, holder.not_held_in the quarters with
    none. With holder the response is lean unless detail="full".
  - "Who are the largest holders / who bought or sold most last quarter?" -> top_holders,
    biggest_buyers, biggest_sellers, largest_new_positions, largest_exits.
  - "Who owns more than 5%?" -> large_holders_5pct (latest 13D/13G per holder).

quarters[] is newest complete quarter first (the one still being filed is
in_progress_quarter), each with holders, shares_held, value_usd and share_classes[] (per
cover-page class: shares_outstanding, held_by_13f, pct_of_class), share_count_source and
holders_url.

Report each share class separately; never add classes together. Caveats to state: 13F is as
filed and not deduplicated, options are excluded, holdings can exceed 100% for heavily
shorted stocks, and a "new position" may be a manager whose previous 13F was late. Cite
share_count_source for share counts and holders_url for holdings.

Args:
    company: Ticker (e.g. "AMD") or CIK of the company being held (not of the institution); for a
        company name, get them from search_companies first
    quarters: Number of complete quarters, newest first (1-12, default 4)
    holder: Optional 13F filer to follow across the quarters: a name fragment ("Baupost",
        "Berkshire") or a CIK ("1061768")
    limit: Number of top holders to return for the latest quarter (1-100, default 25)
    detail: "lean" or "full". Default: lean when holder is given (just the holder's positions,
        share classes and sources), full otherwise (adds top holders, buyers, sellers, new
        positions, exits and 5%+ holders)
    ticker: Same as company (models often name it so)
    cik: Same as company

A ticker that cannot be tied to a company (an index option such as XSP, a former ticker) is
not an error: the response has empty quarters and not_covered with the reason, and
ticker_used_by names companies whose cover pages stated it.
name: get_institutional_holders
title: Get Institutional Holders
